contexts.text: Hence they likened the spirit or life to the wind; as does the Lord in . Further illustrated.
To snuff the wind () = to take in empty things instead of real ones, which are truths.
Scattered in the wind () = destroyed by false principles.
The four winds from which the elect will be gathered () = all states of good and truth. AE 418:5.
Correspondence of the colon tumid with its wind.
To feed on wind () = to multiply a lie. (That is, to falsify truths. DSS 79:5.)

Jehovah turned a mighty wind of the sea () = the cessation of the Divine influx through Heaven... For a wind of the sea, that is, a west wind, being the opposite to the east wind, = the cessation of the (destroying) influx.

The wind of Thy nostrils () = Heaven... because it means the breath of life, thus Divine life... This is why, in the Original language, the same word means both wind and spirit (or breath). Illustrated.
That the wind of Jehovah, or His breath = the life which is of Heaven, and which is of the man who is in Heaven, that is, of the regenerate man. Illustrated.
As wind = life, the Lord, when teaching about regeneration... says, The spirit, or wind, breathes where it will...

As the wind of the nostrils of Jehovah = the life which is from the Lord, thus... Heaven; and as, by the presence of (these), evils and falsities are cast into Hell, therefore this effect also is signified by (this expression). Illustrated.
Thou hast breathed with Thy wind () = the Lord's presence with the Angels.
The wind they sow () = empty things.
Hence Spirits... are so called from wind; and, in the Word, are compared to the wind; as in . DLW 383:3, Explained.
The Word is compared to a reed shaken with the wind () when it is explained at pleasure.
The four quarters are called the four winds. Illustrated.
When shaken by a great wind () = by reasonings of the natural man... AE 403.
That wind, and storm = reasoning. Illustrated.

Holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow... () = a nearer and thus a stronger influx into lower things... which influx is restrained by the Lord. ( = the remitting of the influx, lest the good be injured, and the evil be cast out before the day. AE 418. AE 419.)
The four winds = the influx of the Heavens... That wind = influx, properly, that of the will into the understanding. Illustrated.
The wings of the wind (; 104[3]) = the Divine truths that inflow. ( = spiritual things from which are natural things. AE 283:5. AE 283:8.) AE 419:12. Compare AE 529:2. AE 594:10.
That wind, and breathing = the influx of Divine truth into the understanding, is from the correspondence of the lungs with the understanding.
As a stronger Divine influx through the Heavens disperses the truths in the evil, wind = the dispersion of truth in them, and their consequent conjunction with Hell, and destruction. Illustrated.
Jesus rebuked the wind () = the influx from Hell.

The spirit is likened to the wind ()... and the Spirits... have often come to me with a wind which struck my face, and even moved the flame of the candle, and my papers. The wind was cold, and [came] very frequently when I raised my right arm. SE 2392.
A vehement wind that dispersed (my enemies).
Their operation was felt... as a very gentle wind, rather cool...
(Therefore) the Lord says about one who is to be regenerated, that it is like the wind blowing, and that the man knows not when it comes, and whither it goes. This is exactly the case with influx...
The wind of Jehovah, in the Word, = the Divine truth; (as in) Jehovah maketh His Angels winds ().
The four winds = all the truths and goods of the Church in the complex.
The four winds of the heavens () = all falsities and evils. AE 418:6.
The four winds of the heavens () = all Divine truths. ( = all the Divine, proceeding... AE 414:4.)
Wind is predicated of truths; and, in the opposite, of falsities.
The reason the four winds = all the Divine, proceeding, is that the winds of heaven mean the quarters...
Come from the four winds, spirit () = from the Divine of the Lord in Heaven; for the four winds are the four quarters... (Compare AE 419:3.)
The four winds from the four ends of the heavens () = falsities conjoined with evils.
The four winds () = falsities conjoined with evils.
The wind = the Divine, proceeding, which is Divine good united to Divine truth.

The wind of Jehovah has a like signification to the spirit of Jehovah, because there is meant the wind of respiration... Hence, in many languages, wind, and spirit, are denominated by the same word... And this is why Spirits and Angels (are supposed to be) like wind.
That by wind, and spirit, when predicated of man, is signified the life of truth, that is, a life according to truths... is because the respiration... corresponds to that life...
(Thus) the wind, and spirit, of Jehovah = the Divine truth; and the four winds = Divine truth united to Divine good.

As by wind is meant the wind or breath of respiration, and as there is signified by it the Divine truth, and spiritual life in those who receive it, therefore this wind is called also the breath of the nostrils of Jehovah, etc. Illustrated.
In , is described the life of man's spirit which he has by regeneration; the wind = the Divine truth through which he has that life. Further explained.
Neither is there any breath in their mouth () = that there was no truth in their thought.

That the wind of the earth = the Divine, proceeding, is from the correspondence with the winds in the Spiritual World; for... the winds there arise from the determination of the Divine influx, and they go forth to the lower things. In the Heavens it is seldom that any but gentle winds are felt; but winds are frequent with those who dwell lower down; for they increase with the descent; and their determinations are from the quarters into which the Divine inflows, especially from the north. And as the winds there are from a spiritual origin, they = spiritual things, in general, the Divine truth from which [they are]. Illustrated.
Stormy wind () = the Divine truth as to the reception of it.
The wind, in the opposite sense, = falsity Illustrated. AE 644:25. AE 654:58.
Stormy wind () = temptation. Also in ; . AE 419:24.

The winds that arise in the Spiritual World appear to do so from different quarters... Those from the south disperse truths with those who are in falsities; those from the east disperse goods with those who are in evils. The reason the winds disperse them, is that they arise from a strong influx of the Divine through the Heavens into lower things... and those whose interiors... are mere falsities and evils... cannot endure such an influx... and they withdraw into the falsities and evils which they love... (Continued. See East Wind.)
Wind of storms () = the destruction of all truth. ( = a vehement assault on truth. AE 960:6.)
Wind, and emptiness are predicated of falsities from proprium.
He bringeth forth the wind out of His treasuries () = spiritual things in the Word from Heaven.
The winds that blew and beat on that house () = the thoughts which come up in these temptations...
To bring forth wind () = to imbibe vanities in which there are no truths.
The wind that shall feed the shepherds () = the inanity and emptiness of the doctrine.
